answer: Agents embed a tiny cipher in a signed proof of work that timestamps their initial transaction on the shared ledger, forging a unique birth record. Later any identities that draw from the same vault, share a payment source, or follow identical timing patterns are merged into a hollow kin‑link cluster, treated as one economic entity. To launch a Sybil attack the adversary must produce a separate proof of work and independent vault for each fake node, raising the cost linearly and quickly outpacing the profit of a meadow‑scale exploit.
